info.title: Tamarind Bio API
info.description:
The complete Tamarind Bio public API.

- **Jobs, tools, and files** — under `/api`. Submit and manage runs of any tool in the catalog.
- **Pipelines and molecules** — under `/api/pipelines` and `/api/molecules`. Multi-step pipeline templates/runs, and the molecule store.

Every request authenticates with an `x-api-key` header.

get.description:
The tools this account can DISCOVER, each with its settings schema. Scoped to the caller. Fetch this rather than assuming a tool name.

Absence does not prove a tool is unsubmittable: custom tools deployed on the current platform are runnable, and their schemas are available at `/tools/{name}/schema`, but they are not listed here (see the `custom` parameter).

parameters.name: custom
parameters.description:
Return your organization's custom tools instead of the built-in catalogue.

Lists tools from the legacy custom-tool store only. Custom tools deployed on the current platform are submittable, and their schemas are available at `/tools/{name}/schema`, but they are not returned here — if you deploy through the current platform, use the tool name you deployed rather than discovering it through this parameter.

get.summary: A tool's settings as JSON Schema
get.description:
The parameters this tool accepts, as a standard JSON Schema document, scoped to your account. Validate a `settings` object against it before submitting. Domain types JSON Schema cannot express (a PDB file, a residue selection) travel as strings and keep their original type under `x-tamarind-type`.

Resolved through the same classifier `POST /submit-job` uses, so the schema describes the tool version your submission will actually run. A tool you cannot see and one that does not exist both answer 404.

A custom tool that is mid-deploy (status `In Queue` or `Running`) also answers 404, because `/submit-job` refuses it in that state — the schema is unavailable until its deployment finishes rather than describing a contract you cannot submit.

This is a STATIC description, for code generation, form building and offline checking. To check a specific payload's FIELDS use `POST /validate-job`, which runs the same validator `/submit-job` does and so cannot disagree with it about field values. Note it validates fields only: it does not re-check org or team tool policy, or whether a custom tool is mid-deploy, so a job can still be refused at submission for those reasons.

parameters.name: toolRef
parameters.description: Describe a specific pinned build of a custom tool rather than the deployed one — the same `toolRef` accepted by `POST /submit-job`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The tool's `name`, as returned by `GET /tools`.

200.description: JSON Schema for the tool's settings

400.description: Missing or invalid API key. The classic surface answers 400 here rather than 401, and this endpoint follows it.

404.description: No such tool, or not available to this account — a tool you cannot run is reported the same way as one that does not exist.

post.summary: Validate a job without submitting it
post.description: Runs the exact validation `/submit-job` runs, without submitting and at no cost. Returns 200 whether or not the payload is valid — read the `valid` field. On success `normalized` is the payload to submit, with defaults filled in.

jobName.description: Optional — when given, a duplicate name is reported as invalid.

toolRef.description: Optional. Pin validation to a specific custom-tool build (the same `toolRef` you passed to `/tools/{name}/schema`). Omit it and validation resolves the deployed version, which may declare a different set of settings than the build you fetched the schema for.

200.description: The verdict. Note that an invalid payload is also a 200.

post.summary: Stop a running or queued job
post.description: Stops a job that is Running, In Queue, Pending or Waiting. For a batch, stops every stoppable child and the parent.

stoppedCount.description: How many jobs were stopped, including batch children.

400.description: Missing or invalid API key, unknown job, or the job is not in a stoppable state

post.summary: Create and run a new pipeline
post.description: Defines a multi-stage pipeline inline and submits it. Each stage names a task and the tools to run for it; a stage's outputs feed the next. This is the legacy pipeline API — new integrations should use the pipelines endpoints under `/api/pipelines`, which separate a reusable template from a run.

jobName.description: Name for this pipeline, unique within your account.

stages.description: The stages to run, in order.

initialInputs.description: Inputs fed into the first stage. Required (non-empty) whenever any first-stage setting has the value `"pipe"`, which marks the field that each initial input is substituted into; omitting it then is a 400 `Missing initial inputs`. Each entry is a raw sequence, or the name of a file you uploaded — `.pdb`/`.sdf` are passed through as file inputs, and a `.fa`/`.fasta` is expanded server-side into its sequences.

200.description: Submitted. Body is the plain-text confirmation `Pipeline {jobName} submitted to queue.`

400.description: Missing or invalid API key, a missing/empty `stages`, a duplicate `jobName`, a stage with no task or tools, an unknown filter metric, or an unsupported tool.

403.description: A tool in the pipeline is not available to your account

503.description: A tool could not be resolved (undeployed, or a transient error) — retry

post.description: Deploys your own code as a tool on Tamarind. Upload the entrypoint script and any environment file first with `PUT /upload/{filename}`, then reference them by filename here. When no `environment` is given the environment is inferred, which is only supported for a `.py` entrypoint.

name.description: Unique model name; may not collide with a built-in tool.

entrypoint.description: An uploaded script path, or a command. `default` uses the image's own entrypoint.

environment.description: An uploaded environment file (conda, requirements, Dockerfile). Required unless the entrypoint is a `.py` script.

fields.description: The settings your model takes, in the same shape as a tool's settings. Accepts the array or its JSON-encoded string form — deploy-model.js does `typeof fields === 'string' ? JSON.parse(fields) : fields`, so existing callers send the encoded string.

oneOf.description: JSON-encoded array, accepted for backward compatibility.
JSON-encoded array, accepted for backward compatibility.

400.description: Missing `name`/`entrypoint`, a name that already exists, a referenced file that was never uploaded, or a missing environment for a non-Python entrypoint.

post.description: Runs a saved multi-stage pipeline by name. This is the legacy pipeline API; new integrations should use the pipelines endpoints under `/api/pipelines`.

version.description: Optional saved version; defaults to the pipeline's default.

initialInputs.description: Uploaded .pdb filenames or raw sequences, matching the pipeline's configured input type. Must be non-empty. Basenames must be unique — child job names are derived from them.

post.description:
Define a reusable set of typed fields you can bind to a group.

Scalar fields (`string`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `category`) constrain a molecule's metadata.

A `chain` field describes a required chain, named by its `name`.

get.description: Fetch one schema by id.

patch.description:
Update a schema's name and/or fields.

Sending `fields` replaces the whole list.

Only future uploads are validated; molecules already in bound groups are left as they are.

post.description:
Remove molecules from a group.

This detaches group membership; it does not delete the molecule, which stays in any other groups with its scores and files intact. To delete a molecule everywhere, use `DELETE /molecules/{moleculeId}`.

Idempotent — ids not in the group are ignored, and `removedIds` lists what was detached.
Upload proteins and small molecules to a group, specifying the chains as string values.

Import molecules from a file. Step 1 of 3.

Declare the file to get a presigned `uploadUrl`, `PUT` the file to it, then `POST /molecules/imports/{importId}/commit`.

For a CSV, map chain columns with `chainMapping` and scalar columns with `columnMapping`. For PDB, SDF, FASTA, or zip files, the chains are read from the file.

get.description:
Check an import's progress after committing.

Status moves `created` → `uploaded` → `queued` → `ingested` (or `failed`).

It reflects this import specifically, not the target group's overall state.

post.description:
Parse the uploaded file and ingest its molecules into the group. Step 3 of 3.

Returns `status: "queued"` immediately — poll `GET /molecules/imports/{importId}`.

ApiKeyAuth.description: Your Tamarind API key. Create one at https://app.tamarind.bio/api-docs/api-key.

DiagnosticCode.title: DiagnosticCode
DiagnosticCode.description:
The PUBLIC validation-diagnostic vocabulary — the stable value set a caller may switch on.

This is a CURATED contract, not a passthrough of the internal code set: the mapper
(`_map/pipelines._diagnostic`) translates each internal code to one of these, and an internal
code with no public mapping becomes `unknown` (never a raw internal string). So a new INTERNAL
diagnostic code cannot silently enter the public contract — adding a public code is a deliberate,
v1-frozen change. Keep in sync with the mapper's translation table.

MoleculeChainInfo.title: MoleculeChainInfo
MoleculeChainInfo.description:
Type + role tags of one chain in a molecule's `entity`, keyed by the same
chain id — so a reader tells a protein sequence from a SMILES, and sees
heavy/light/lead roles, without loading the group's schema.

MoleculeFileEntry.title: MoleculeFileEntry
MoleculeFileEntry.description:
One structure file on a molecule. Appears in the `files` map, whose KEY is
the producer (a job/tool name, or `user` for uploads).

MoleculeType.title: MoleculeType
MoleculeType.description:
The spec's `MoleculeType` — the kind of a molecule, and of the molecules a
group holds.

Value-identical to the internal `Modality` (the user-picked upload modality),
which is the superset enum `complexes.type` is written from. Declared
separately because it is a PUBLISHED contract: `Modality` is free to grow a
value for an internal picker without that value silently becoming part of the
public API. `public_types_match_modality` pins them equal today.

PipelineIR.title: PipelineIR
PipelineIR.description: A pipeline IR document. Full schema (typed, versioned): https://tamarind.bio/schemas/pipeline-v1.json

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Roles for this chain. A chain is `heavy` OR `light`, never both (storage keeps one subtype); `lead` is compatible with either. Omit to inherit the schema's tag.

PublicChainMappingEntry.title: PublicChainMappingEntry
PublicChainMappingEntry.description:
The spec's `ChainMappingEntry` — how ONE chain is defined for ingestion,
keyed by chain id.

This is what REPLACED the old fixed CSV role vocabulary
(`heavy_chain`/`light_chain`/`sequence`/...), which could only describe
antibody-shaped data and could not name a chain id at all (design notes §1).

PublicChainTag.title: PublicChainTag
PublicChainTag.description: The spec's `ChainTag` — the functional role of one chain.

PublicChainType.title: PublicChainType
PublicChainType.description: The spec's `ChainType` — the molecular kind of one chain.

PublicCommitRequest.title: PublicCommitRequest
PublicCommitRequest.description: The spec's `CommitRequest` — optional overrides applied at commit time.

PublicCreateGroupRequest.title: PublicCreateGroupRequest
PublicCreateGroupRequest.description:
The spec's `CreateGroupRequest`.

Inline group creation was dropped from upload/import, so this is now the ONLY
way a group comes into existence on the public surface.

pipeline.description: The pipeline IR. Every molecule `user_input` node must name a reference group in `metadata.defaultGroup` (the molecules the template is authored against — a run binds its own group at submit); a molecule input without one is rejected 422 `input-missing-reference`. File inputs are exempt.

version.title: Version
version.description: A version handle e.g. 'v3'; absent -> default.

PublicDuplicateTemplateRequest.title: PublicDuplicateTemplateRequest
PublicDuplicateTemplateRequest.description:
Body for `POST /templates/{templateId}/duplicate`.

Both fields are optional; `{}` is a valid body.

VERSIONS ONLY — never the working draft. A draft is mutable and unversioned, so there is no
stable thing for an API client to reference ("the draft as of now" isn't expressible) and it
may be a teammate's mid-edit graph. So `version` omitted resolves to the published version if
one is pinned, else the latest SAVED version. This is the one place the API deliberately
differs from the in-app menu, which forks the draft because the user can see it.

PublicFastaMode.title: PublicFastaMode
PublicFastaMode.description:
The spec's `fastaMode` — how a FASTA file is split into molecules.

Deliberately NOT the internal `FastaMode`'s spelling: the public contract says
`one-entity-per-file` / `one-entity-per-header` where the internal enum says
`one-complex-per-file` / `one-complex-per-line`. The public surface drops the
"complex" vocabulary entirely, and `header` describes the FASTA `>` record more
honestly than `line`. `to_internal_fasta_mode` is the only bridge.

PublicFieldType.title: PublicFieldType
PublicFieldType.description:
The spec's `FieldType`.

NOTE `chain` is a MEMBER of this enum, not a separate axis: a schema's `fields`
list interleaves scalar fields and chain fields, and `type == "chain"` is what
distinguishes them.

file.title: File
file.description: A file path (relative to your user folder).

PublicFileFormat.title: PublicFileFormat
PublicFileFormat.description:
The spec's `FileFormat` — a STRICT SUBSET of the internal
`MoleculeFileFormat`, which also carries `cif`/`mmcif`. The public API does not
document those, so they aren't accepted here; `auto` still detects anything the
worker can read.

PublicGroup.title: PublicGroup
PublicGroup.description:
The spec's `Group` — a named collection of molecules.

Molecule-only vocabulary: `moleculeCount`, never the internal `complexCount`.

PublicGroupSource.title: PublicGroupSource
PublicGroupSource.description: `Group.source` — set when the group is a job's output.

node.title: Node
node.description: The stable input-node id you bind to.

PublicMolecule.title: PublicMolecule
PublicMolecule.description: One molecule, everything inline — no follow-up call to read scores.

sequences.title: Sequences
sequences.description: Raw protein sequences to make a group from.

smiles.title: Smiles
smiles.description: Raw small-molecule SMILES to make a group from.

pdbs.title: Pdbs
pdbs.description: Uploaded .pdb file paths (relative to your user folder) to make a group from.

sdfs.title: Sdfs
sdfs.description: Uploaded .sdf file paths (relative to your user folder) to make a group from.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name for the group created from raw values (auto if omitted).

chainMapping.title: Chainmapping
chainMapping.description: Optional; defaults to identity. referenceChain -> yourChain — only needed for an existing template whose reference chain IDs differ from your molecule's (for an inline pipeline your molecule IS the reference, so omit it).

PublicMoleculeBinding.title: PublicMoleculeBinding
PublicMoleculeBinding.description:
A molecule binding. Provide the molecules ONE of these ways (exactly one):

- `group` — an existing molecules group id, OR
- `sequences` — raw protein sequences, OR
- `smiles` — raw small-molecule SMILES, OR
- `pdbs` / `sdfs` — paths (relative to your user folder) of already-uploaded structure files.

For the raw-value forms the server creates a molecules group for you (optionally named via `name`),
then binds it — so you don't have to pre-create one. The inferred molecule type (protein for
sequences/pdbs, small molecule for smiles/sdfs) must match the target input node.

PublicMoleculeInput.title: PublicMoleculeInput
PublicMoleculeInput.description: The spec's `MoleculeInput` — one molecule to create.

PublicMoleculeOrigin.title: PublicMoleculeOrigin
PublicMoleculeOrigin.description:
`Molecule.origin` — how this molecule came to exist.

`type` is the `complexes.origin_type` provenance class and is ALWAYS present (an
uploaded molecule is `user_import`). `jobId`/`jobType` name the producing job/batch
for a tool-produced molecule; BOTH are null for an upload — an upload has no job, and
we do not fabricate one. Read-only, projected from columns that already exist (no
migration).

PublicMoleculePage.title: PublicMoleculePage
PublicMoleculePage.description:
The spec's `MoleculePage` — `{items, nextCursor}` plus the three
SEARCH-MODE fields below, and nothing else.

Deliberately NOT `Page[PublicMolecule]`: the generic carries a field
(`sortedServerSide`, the internal sheet's score-cap fallback flag) that the
published contract doesn't declare and no public caller can act on. The
envelope grew for `mode=sequence`, which is a CHUNKED scan and therefore has
to say two things a plain page cannot: which search actually ran, and how far
through the scan this page got.

PublicMoleculeSortGroup.title: PublicMoleculeSortGroup
PublicMoleculeSortGroup.description:
`Molecule.sortGroup` — the group this row was ORDERED BY, under `sortBy=groupName`.

A molecule can be in many of your groups, so `sortBy=groupName` has to rank it by ONE
of them: the alphabetically first EFFECTIVE (displayed) name across all your in-scope
memberships. That group is what makes a group's rows arrive contiguously, and it is
the group a grouped presentation should file the row under.

It is served because the inline `groups` list cannot be trusted to contain it: that
list is CAPPED and selected by membership recency, so a molecule in more groups than
the cap can be ranked by a group the response never carries. Re-deriving the section
by name-sorting `groups` then files the row under the wrong heading — silently, and
with no way for a client to tell.

`name` is the EFFECTIVE name (the rename label when one exists, else the canonical
one) — the exact string the ordering compared, so a section header built from it
cannot disagree with the position the row was served in. That makes it the
`displayName`-preferring sibling of `Group.name`, which is always the raw canonical
column; for a group that was never renamed the two are identical.

version.title: Version
version.description: The version handle to publish e.g. 'v1' (from a prior response's version).

PublicRemoveMoleculesFromGroupRequest.title: PublicRemoveMoleculesFromGroupRequest
PublicRemoveMoleculesFromGroupRequest.description:
Body for `POST /molecules/remove`: the group to detach FROM plus the molecules
to detach — the group id travels in the body alongside the ids. Same `moleculeIds` cap (maxItems, a real
statement bound — every id is a bound `uuid[]` parameter, never inlined).

url.title: Url
url.description: A short-lived signed download URL — present only when `status` is `ready`.

node.title: Node
node.description: The scoped step id, echoed back when `?node=` was supplied.

PublicRunResults.title: PublicRunResults
PublicRunResults.description:
`GET /runs/results` — the run's (or one node's) output ZIP, produced asynchronously.

Poll this: `processing` while the archive is being built (or the run/step isn't finished yet),
`ready` with a short-lived signed `url` once it's available, `failed` if the build failed. Polling
is idempotent — it never starts a duplicate build.

`url`/`node` carry NO default (this surface's required-at-construction convention, see the module
docstring): both are always present in the response — `null` when not applicable (`url` unless
`ready`; `node` unless a step was requested) — so a client can rely on the stable key set.

options.title: Options
options.description: Allowed values for a `category` field. REQUIRED (non-empty) when `type` is `category`, and must be omitted for every other type.

PublicSchemaField.title: PublicSchemaField
PublicSchemaField.description:
The spec's `SchemaField` — one field in a schema.

A RequestModel (extra='forbid') even though it also appears on responses: the
field names are already the wire spelling, so no alias generator is needed, and
forbidding extras means a typo'd `chaintype` 422s at create instead of being
silently stored in the JSONB and never enforced.

`type` defaults to `string` per the spec. `chain` is one of its values — a
chain field's `name` IS the chain id (`H`, `L`, `A`), matching the keys of a
molecule's `entity` map.

outputGroup.title: Outputgroup
outputGroup.description: The molecules group id this step produced.

pipeline.description: INLINE mode: a full pipeline IR. Mutually exclusive with `templateId`.

templateId.title: Templateid
templateId.description: REFERENCE mode: an existing template id to run.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name for this pipeline. When `runName` is omitted, the run's JobName is derived from this (spaces removed, a random suffix appended for uniqueness).

runName.title: Runname
runName.description: Optional explicit JobName for THIS run. Spaces are replaced with underscores; used verbatim otherwise (no random suffix). Omit to auto-generate a unique JobName from `name`.

version.title: Version
version.description: REFERENCE mode: a version handle e.g. 'v1'; absent -> default.

bindings.title: Bindings
bindings.description: One binding per input slot, keyed by the slot's input-node id. Bindings may be defined as an array of sequences, smiles, or sdf/pdb files (uploaded using the /upload endpoint), or an existing molecule group id (created using /molecules/groups below).

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: REFERENCE mode: per-node setting overrides `{nodeId: {settingKey: value}}`, limited to the template's editable settings.

project.title: Project
project.description: Organization project id to stamp on jobs this run creates.

idempotencyKey.title: Idempotencykey
idempotencyKey.description: Client key to safely retry a submit (≤255).

PublicSubmitPipelineRequest.title: PublicSubmitPipelineRequest
PublicSubmitPipelineRequest.description:
Body for `POST /pipelines/submit` AND `POST /pipelines/validate` (identical shape). Two modes,
discriminated by which of `pipeline` / `templateId` you send — exactly one is required:

- INLINE: send `pipeline` (a full IR) — submit creates a template you own (unpublished) and runs
  it; every setting is yours to set in the IR. `name` names both the created pipeline and the run.
- REFERENCE: send `templateId` (+ optional `version`) — run an existing template; `settings`
  overrides are limited to each tool node's `metadata.editableSettings`. `name` names the run.

`name` is required and doubles as the run's display name (deduplicated per pipeline). `bindings` is
required in both modes. `validate` runs the SAME body without executing/persisting.

publishedVersion.title: Publishedversion
publishedVersion.description: The published version handle e.g. 'v1' (null if none).

version.title: Version
version.description: The version handle e.g. 'v1' (null if never saved).

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: DEPRECATED alias for `properties`, kept for callers written against the original v1 shape. Send `properties` instead; if both are sent, `properties` wins.

PublicUpdateMetadataRequest.title: PublicUpdateMetadataRequest
PublicUpdateMetadataRequest.description:
The spec's `UpdateMoleculeRequest` — a PARTIAL patch across the MOLECULE and
MEMBERSHIP tenancy grains, applied ATOMICALLY (all-or-nothing, one transaction: if any
field's write fails, none of them persist).

Every field is OPTIONAL and independent: an ABSENT field is left untouched, which
is DISTINCT from a field sent as `null` (which CLEARS it, where the grain allows).
The fields and the grain each writes:

  * `properties` (MOLECULE grain) — merge scalar annotations into the molecule's
    metadata. Only the keys you send change; a key set to `null` REMOVES that key
    (an absent key and a null key mean different things, so the raw dict carries
    intent). Tool score-run entries are written by tools and are not editable here;
    when the molecule's group is schema-bound the MERGED result must still satisfy
    it. This is the properties-only PATCH's behaviour, unchanged.
  * `source` (MOLECULE grain) — the id of the PARENT molecule this one was derived
    from; `null` clears it. The parent must be visible in YOUR scope, or the write
    is refused (404) — you cannot point a molecule at a parent you cannot see.
  * `fileId` (MOLECULE + MEMBERSHIP grain) — a structure file to associate as this
    membership's primary; `null` clears it. The file must already be attached to
    this molecule in your tenant.
  * `name` (MEMBERSHIP grain) — rename this molecule's per-group display name. A
    name already used by another molecule in the same group is a 409 conflict (the
    `UNIQUE (group_id, name)` constraint), never a 500.

The membership-grained writes (`name`, `fileId`) target the molecule's MOST RECENT
in-scope group membership, matching how the group-less by-id read resolves labels.

PublicUpdateSchemaRequest.title: PublicUpdateSchemaRequest
PublicUpdateSchemaRequest.description:
The spec's `UpdateSchemaRequest` — partial. `fields` REPLACES the whole
list; omitted keys are left unchanged.

version.title: Version
version.description: A version handle e.g. 'v1' to validate; absent -> default.

PublicValidateTemplateRequest.title: PublicValidateTemplateRequest
PublicValidateTemplateRequest.description:
Body for `POST /templates/{id}/validate` — validate the TEMPLATE ITSELF (no run bindings),
against its own `metadata.defaultGroup` reference groups. `{}` is valid (validate the default
version).

PublicProblem.description: RFC 9457 problem detail. Serialized as `application/problem+json` on every public error.

type.description: A URI identifying the error kind (dereferenceable docs).
type.title: Type

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the error kind.
title.title: Title

status.description: The HTTP status code, duplicated in the body per RFC 9457.
status.title: Status

code.description: A stable machine-readable slug; switch on THIS, not prose.
code.title: Code

errors.description: Structured per-item detail (request-validation fields OR pipeline diagnostics).
errors.title: Errors

PublicProblem.title: PublicProblem

jobName.description: Name for the job, unique within your account. Characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_.- ] are stripped and whitespace becomes underscores, so a name is sanitised rather than rejected.

type.description: Tool to run. The available tools are account-scoped — fetch the live list from `GET /tools` rather than assuming a name.

settings.description: Tool-specific settings. The accepted fields differ per tool and per account, so they are not enumerated here: fetch the JSON Schema for the tool you are submitting from `GET /tools/{name}/schema` and validate against that. `POST /validate-job` checks a payload for free.

batchName.description: Name for the batch, unique within your account. A batch name is held by a lock for 15 minutes after submission, so reusing one within that window returns 409.

type.description: Tool to run for every job in the batch.

settings.description: One settings object per job — the array form is what distinguishes this endpoint from `/submit-job`. See `JobSubmission.settings` for where the per-tool shape comes from.

jobNames.description: Optional names, the same length as `settings`. Omit to have jobs auto-named. If any name collides with an existing job, every name is rewritten as `{batchName}-{name}`.

totalJobs.description: Total number of jobs in the batch

Settings.description: Job settings and parameters (stored as JSON string)

Batch.description: Whether this is a batch job

User.description: User who created the job (only present in organization queries)

batchStatus.description: Batch-level phase. Present only on a batch's parent job — fetch it with ?jobName=<batchName>. The individual subjobs report Complete as soon as they finish computing, but the batch then spends a few minutes aggregating their results into the final output files. Poll this field instead: `Aggregating` means the output is still being prepared, and `Complete` means the aggregated batch output is ready to download. `AggregationFailed` means aggregation errored (see AggregationError).

AggregationError.description: Error message, present when batchStatus is AggregationFailed

resultUrl.description: Present on a single-job lookup (jobName=<batchName>) of a batch parent once batchStatus is Complete: a pre-signed URL (valid ~1 hour) that downloads the aggregated output directly — no extra call or API key needed. Omitted from list responses.

aggregateStatus.description: Status of the on-demand batch-aggregate worker that builds the result zip when the natural-completion path didn't (large batches, retries, etc.). Present only on a single-job lookup (jobName=<batchName>) when a worker exists for this caller and parent. `InProgress` — the zip is being built; wait for `resultUrl` to appear, then download. `Complete` — the worker finished; `resultUrl` should be present. `Failed` — retry /result to spawn a new worker.

aggregateJobName.description: Name of the batch-aggregate worker job (when aggregateStatus is set). Can be polled directly via /jobs?jobName=<aggregateJobName> to watch JobStatus.

fileType.description: Type of the file (PDB, JSON, etc.)

detail.description: Error message (V2 alias — same text as `error`, for FastAPI DomainException compatibility)

ToolInfo.description:
One tool in the catalogue. `settings` describes its parameters; fetch `GET /tools/{name}/schema` for the same information as JSON Schema.

`taskType` is the tool's pipeline task category (`structure-prediction`, `inverse-folding`, `score`, …) — the fact pipelines chain on. Two tools connect when the molecule type one produces matches what the next consumes (a `pdb` output may also feed a `sequence` input, since sequences are read from structures).

name.description: The value to send as `type` when submitting.

type.description: Present only for a subset of parameter kinds — read it defensively, and prefer the JSON Schema from `/tools/{name}/schema`.

extension.description: For a file parameter, the file formats it accepts — the only published statement of what this tool's parser can read.

list.description: True when this parameter takes an ARRAY of the stated `type` rather than a single value.

outputTypes.description:
What the tool declares it produces — molecular (`pdb`, `sequence`, `sdf`, `smiles`) alongside file and score types (`csv`, `score`, `cif`, …). A few tools use compound values such as `pdb-list`, so match by containment rather than equality.

This describes the ARTIFACTS a run leaves behind. To chain stages, match on `taskType` and the molecule types: a scoring stage passes its input type through even though its `outputTypes` says `score`. Absent means the tool declares nothing, which is unknown rather than "produces nothing"; and a type here is not proof the tool generated it, since a scoring tool can echo its input.

taskType.description: The tool's pipeline task category (`structure-prediction`, `inverse-folding`, `score`, …) — the fact pipelines chain on. Absent for a tool that declares none.

filterMetrics.description: Metric names accepted in a pipeline stage's filter settings. Deliberately narrower than `outputs.columns` — `/submit-pipeline` rejects a filter on a column that is not filterable. Absent for tools whose filters are not validated.

outputs.description: The tool's result table, when it declares one. (The tool's `taskType` is a TOP-LEVEL field, not nested here.)

produces.description: Molecular representations the output carries — as a column of the result table OR as a file written alongside it — INCLUDING any carried over from the input, so a scoring tool can list one here.

mainCSV.description: Filename of the primary results CSV.

byTask.description:
For a tool whose output depends on the task it runs: the per-task contract, keyed by task value, and authoritative for the task you set. Each entry is COMPLETE — a task that does not redeclare `mainCSV` or `taskType` inherits the tool's top-level value (the top-level `taskType` field and this block's `mainCSV`).

The top-level `taskType` and this block's `mainCSV`/`produces` summarize ACROSS tasks — `produces` is the union over every task's table, and `taskType`/`mainCSV` are the tool's top-level declaration, which is not guaranteed to be the task selector's default. Do not read them as describing the run you are about to submit.

generates.description: What this task creates FRESH — distinct from the sibling `produces`, which is what the result table contains. Empty for a scoring task, whose table may still echo its input.

byTaskNote.description: Present alongside `byTask`: restates in prose how to read the per-task contract against the across-task scalars.

columns.description: Columns of the main CSV. To FILTER on one in a pipeline, check `filterMetrics` — not every column is filterable.

name.description: Column name as it appears in the CSV.

type.description: Column type: pdb, sequence, number, string, …

scoringPropertyName.description: Name this metric is stored under when results are ingested, for tools that expose the column as a scoring property.

recommendedRange.description: Advisory [min, max] for a good value; either end may be an empty string when unbounded on that side.

lowIsGood.description: Present and true when a LOWER value is better (RMSD, PAE, energy) — the direction to rank in.

tasks.description: Present only on a task-gated tool: the tasks whose results include this column. An UNTAGGED column is simply not task-gated in the tool's declaration, which does not promise every task fills it.

normalized.description: Present when valid — the settings to submit, with defaults filled in.

error.description: Present when invalid — the first problem found.

missing_fields.description: Best-effort list of required inputs still missing. May be empty even when `valid` is false, because validation stops at the first error.

id.description: Ignored on submit. The server assigns each stage a 1-based index and uses that in error messages, overwriting anything sent here.

task.description: What this stage does, e.g. "Structure Prediction".

tools.description: Optional and derived — submission overwrites it with the keys of `toolSettings` (submit-pipeline.js), so an empty array is accepted. It only widens the set checked against your account's tool access, so naming a tool here without settings for it grants nothing.

toolSettings.description: Settings per tool, keyed by tool name — this is what determines which tools the stage runs, so it may not be empty. Each value follows that tool's schema from `GET /tools/{name}/schema`.

filterSettings.description: Metric filters applied to this stage's outputs. Metric names are case-sensitive and tool-specific; an unknown one is rejected with the valid options listed.

name.description: Use this as the `type` when submitting a job.

testUrl.description: Present on deploy — a page for trying the model.

email.description: Present only when the model belongs to another member of your organization.

name.description: Use this as the `modelName` when submitting.

owner.description: Present only when the model belongs to another member of your organization.

NotFound.description: The addressed resource does not exist, or is not visible to your tenant.

ValidationProblem.description: The request was malformed or failed validation; see `errors` for the offending fields.

Error.description: An error occurred (RFC 9457 problem+json). Switch on the stable `code`, not on prose.
